title: High Density Si-IPD Technologies as Enabler for High-Performance and Low-Power Consumption Processor Chips
abstract: Voltage regulators are key devices and are part of almost every power electronic system. Indeed, system architects and designers are continuously looking for new topologies and solutions to increase overall efficiency of such devices. Thanks to the latest technology advancements in active and passive components, designers were able to achieve amazing performances. This work will present an overview of key break throughs in passive components with a focus on Silicon capacitors and IPD (Integrated passive devices).
problem: Power delivery networks in high-performance processors require large on-chip capacitance with minimal area footprint; traditional discrete capacitors consume significant board space. Si-IPD (Silicon Integrated Passive Devices) with high-density silicon capacitors integrate voltage regulation directly on-chip.
motivation: Power delivery efficiency and density directly impact processor performance and thermal behavior; on-chip integration of passive elements reduces parasitic inductance and improves voltage delivery quality.
method: High-density Si-IPD technology integrates silicon capacitors and inductors directly into processor chips using specialized fabrication techniques, achieving higher capacitance density than traditional approaches and reducing parasitic resistance and inductance in the power delivery path.
key_novelty: High-density integrated silicon passive devices enabling efficient on-chip power delivery with minimal area overhead.
contributions: High-density silicon capacitor technology for on-chip integration
Integrated passive device architecture reducing PDN parasitic impedance
Improved voltage regulation efficiency and transient response
Demonstrated application to high-performance processor design

metrics.area: reduced board space for PDN components

primary_theme: Integrated silicon passive devices for power delivery
